claims.text: POL-NS-01 is the only clause that makes a no-show fee chargeable, and it is conjunctive - all four limbs must hold. Limb (d) requires the trip record to show termination by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. The trip record shows the driver cancelled this trip at 13:32:40 under DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. POL-NS-01(d) names that code separately and states that it is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider and does not satisfy the limb. On the driver's own chosen reason code the $4.00 fee is not chargeable at all, and on the DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE outcome the clause directs a full refund of the cancellation fee with no driver compensation, with the mis-selected reason code recorded in the ruling's referrals as a driver-education item. That disposes of the charge without the tribunal needing to reach the GPS.

Independently of the reason code, limb (b) fails. POL-NS-02 deems a driver to have arrived only where the trace contains at least three consecutive fixes, each with horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. The code-computed arrival block on the driver's own trace reports qualifying_fix_count of 0 across all 73 driver fixes, and a longest qualifying run of 0 fixes and 0.0 seconds. That is no qualifying in-radius fix anywhere in the 15 minutes before the cancellation, so limb (b) fails and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the fee. The alternative clock limb (b) offers cannot rescue the charge either: it runs only from a first qualifying in-geofence fix, and on the code-computed test there is none. It is no answer that the driver's track records a minimum distance of 19.8 m at some point in the trip - POL-NS-02 turns on qualifying fixes, not on proximity, and the whole of the track runs out to a maximum of 3205.9 m from the pin at speeds up to 41.3 kph.

Even if the judge were to take the driver's own arrival marker at face value, the dwell limb fails on arithmetic. The free waiting period in force for this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, which is 300 seconds - matching the 300 second LARGE_VENUE minimum in the fee schedule, not the 180 second default. The code-computed effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds, measured on longest_run_sec, against a required 300 seconds: a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 a dwell shorter than the free waiting period makes the cancellation fee not chargeable and refundable in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages, so this is a strict-liability refund and no answer about the driver's patience can defeat it.

The one route by which the driver could have added separate in-geofence intervals together is POL-NS-06(i), and it is closed on this record. That limb requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, of an admissible type, covering the pickup road and the waiting window. EV-ADVIS-00403-01 is MISSING - no advisory covers Gateway Dr in this window - and carries weight 0.0; the code-computed accumulation block returns 0 in-geofence intervals and no advisory candidates at all. A MISSING advisory makes limb (i) unavailable and cannot be asserted to excuse a shortfall, and POL-NS-06(ii) is express that no advisory ever reduces the required minimum. The 300 second shortfall therefore stands untouched.

The chat log shows what actually happened. The rider's message sent at 13:27:32 named her exact position - 'taxi stand outside tower b basement 1' - which is the registered pickup point on the trip record (Westgate, 3 Gateway Dr, Jurong East, Taxi Stand Tower B B1, venue VEN-WESTGATE). The driver's reply at 13:28:07 placed him at 'the pickup bay near jem side' and told her to 'come over'; four minutes later he cancelled without moving. On those facts POL-NS-03 gives the rider the full refund, and limb (i) is directly on point: where the rider stated the correct entrance, block or tower in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii)'s pin-ambiguity goodwill is not open either, because it applies only where neither party specified a sub-location and this rider named the stand, the tower and the basement level. POL-NS-04's 120 second exoneration does not apply because the driver did reply, in 35 seconds - and POL-NS-04 itself sends a replied-to mislocation to POL-NS-03.

Any suggestion that the rider was not there is contradicted by her own track on the same artifact as the driver's. The rider track runs from 13:26:52 to 13:32:34 with 39 fixes, all 39 of them qualifying, a mean distance of 11.3 m from the pickup pin and a maximum of only 15.2 m, at a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph. That is squarely inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider presence radius, and it is stationary for the whole window down to the cancellation. The rider was at the pin and never left it; the driver was elsewhere and told her to move to him.

The driver cannot shortcut the geofence test with the platform's own arrival machinery. platform_policy.arrival_marker for this trip is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. POL-NS-12 recognises platform-confirmed arrival only from a GPS_AUTO arrival event carrying the platform's own geofence measurement with wait-timer events, and says in terms that a driver-pressed marker is not covered by it. The 13:26:52 'arrived' event is therefore nothing more than the driver's own assertion, which must be tested under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05 - and it does not survive the POL-NS-02 test set out above.

There is no money for the driver on this record. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Limb (d) fails, and POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 each displace it independently, so the 80 percent payout is never reached. POL-NS-03(i) separately denies compensation where the rider named the tower in chat and the driver did not move to it. Nothing in the driver's profile changes that: the anti-farming check requires no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more and a rate above 0.08, and the driver's figure is 1, so the profile is neither a ground for nor against anyone here.

Nothing on the rider's side of this case is impaired, so no discount applies to the facts that decide it. EV-GPS-00403 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 73 fixes at the 10 second expected cadence, 100 per cent coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 second gap threshold and six-fix threshold are not engaged, and the rider track it relies on is present. EV-TRIP-00403, EV-CHAT-00403 and EV-FARE-00403 are likewise COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the fare ledger's cancellation line of 4.00 reconciles with the net figure of 4.00 read from platform_policy through the fee schedule's resolution rule, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged either. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the deciding facts carry weight 1.0, and nothing here drives confidence to the 0.70 floor.

The sum in issue is exactly $4.00 and there is nothing else on the ledger. The fare breakdown shows a single cancellation_fee line of 4.00 against total_charged of 4.00, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the waiting_time_fee line at 0.00 with no distance, time or platform components. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line, and under POL-GEN-03 a ruling that returns the whole contested amount to the filing party - here the rider - is FULL_REFUND, meaning the present charge is not left standing.

This case should be decided, not deferred. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged: the driver's trace and the trip record are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and are not impaired under any limb of POL-NS-08, so limb (e) does not fire; the reason code in limb (d) of POL-NS-01 decides the charge whatever the arrival facts are, so there is no unresolved conflict of the kind limb (b) describes; and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 with rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d at 0, so limbs (c) and (d) do not fire. Escalation would only hold the $4.00 the rider has already been charged; the record supports a ruling now.

The platform's own trip record, not a reconstruction, places the driver at the pickup from 13:26:52 to the cancellation at 13:32:40 — a recorded wait of 5.8 minutes, i.e. 348 seconds, against the 300-second free waiting period in force for this LARGE_VENUE pickup under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. On the record that levied the fee, the waiting period the rider was charged for was served, and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is met on the platform's own measurement and not merely on the driver's assertion.

The rider's case rests on the derived arrival counter, and that counter does not affirmatively put the driver away from the pickup. The same artifact records the driver's nearest approach to the pin as 19.8 m (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) while its arrival block records zero qualifying in-radius fixes (derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count = 0) against an arrival radius of 120 m for this zone class. Both numbers come from one trace and can be reconciled only by the horizontal-accuracy datum, which this package nowhere publishes; POL-NS-02 provides that a fix with no reported horizontal accuracy is evidence of neither presence nor absence, and the counter therefore cannot be read as a finding that the driver was elsewhere.

Two admissible artifacts, each COMPLETE at weight 1.0, state two different dwell figures — the trip record's 348 recorded seconds and the trace's 0-second longest qualifying run (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec). The clause that would break that tie, POL-NS-05, cannot be run on this package, because it turns on the driver's distance from the pin and his speed at the 13:26:52 arrival marker and the package reports neither. Where two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on dwell and no clause resolves the conflict, POL-NS-09(b) sends the case to a human reviewer and the disputed fee is held rather than refunded while that review is pending.

This is the wrong-face-of-the-venue case POL-NS-03 was written for, not a driver who never came. The venue is recorded with three registered pickup points (trip_record.registered_pickup_points = 3); the rider's own track sits at the pin throughout, 39 of 39 qualifying fixes and never more than 15.17 m from it (derived.rider_presence.max_distance_m); and the driver told the rider in chat that he was at a pickup bay 'near jem side', a bay she was not at. The mislocation is a venue and pin question to be allocated from the chat log, where the driver stated where he was and kept waiting, rather than an absence.

The driver did not leave the rider uncoordinated. Her locating message was sent at 13:27:32 and the driver answered it at 13:28:07, 35 seconds later, telling her where he was; he messaged again at 13:30:52 and she read it at 13:31:12. POL-NS-04 exonerates a rider only where limb (b) holds — no reply within 120 seconds and no in-app call recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls — so limb (b) fails on this chat log and the fee cannot be disposed of on the footing that the driver ignored the rider.

Nothing in the driver's record supports an anti-farming inference. One no-show termination in the trailing 30 days against 120 completed trips is a rate of 0.008, an order of magnitude below the 0.08 that POL-NS-07 requires in addition to a count of 4 or more; both limbs of that check must hold, and neither does. No withholding of any payout is available against this driver, and no escalation under POL-NS-09 is available on the two profile counters POL-GEN-01 permits for this test.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

The fee can only stand if all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, and limb (d) fails. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00403, weight 1.0) shows the driver terminated the trip at 13:32:40 under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE. POL-NS-01(d) names that code and states it is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider; a no-show charge requires RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. On the driver's own chosen reason code the fee is not chargeable.

Limb (b) fails too. POL-NS-02 deems a driver to have arrived only where the trace holds at least three consecutive fixes, each with reported horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better, inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup. EV-GPS-00403 (weight 1.0) reports 0 qualifying in-radius fixes across its 73 driver fixes and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 s. The derived in-geofence dwell is therefore 0.0 s against the 300 s free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 300, EV-TRIP-00403), so POL-NS-06 independently makes the fee refundable in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays the 80% figure ($3.20 of $4.00) only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 each displace it.

The driver's arguments are answered. The recorded wait_time_min of 5.8 min (348 s) is the interval from the driver's own 'arrived' tap at 13:26:52 to the cancellation at 13:32:40, not an in-geofence dwell: POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the marker, and POL-NS-05 does not let a marker start the clock. The arrival block's 0 counter is not neutralised by the unpublished accuracy datum: POL-NS-02 asks for a fix with REPORTED accuracy of 25 m or better, and a fix without one cannot satisfy that test, so the clause's own direction applies (no qualifying in-radius fix means the driver never arrived). There is therefore no conflict of the kind POL-NS-09(b) describes - POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-02 resolve it - and the case is not escalated. The other POL-NS-09 triggers are not engaged: the counterparty-dispute counters are both 0 and the rider's 30-day no-show counter is 0 (limbs (c) and (d)); nothing deciding this case is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d), so limb (e) does not fire; and confidence is above the 0.70 floor, so limb (a) does not fire. The arrival marker is BUTTON, so POL-NS-12 does not apply.

The rider's position is not in doubt: her own track on the same artifact holds 39 qualifying fixes, all stationary, a mean of 11.3 m and a maximum of 15.2 m from the pin, and her 13:27:32 message named the registered pickup point ('taxi stand outside tower b basement 1'). The driver replied at 13:28:07 from a bay 'near jem side' and cancelled without moving. That is a wrong-face-of-the-venue location mismatch, and because the rider named the stand, POL-NS-03(i) would in any event deny the driver compensation; POL-NS-03(ii)'s pin-ambiguity goodwill is not open because she did specify the sub-location. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider - the driver replied within 35 seconds, so its limb (b) fails - but nothing turns on that, because the refund rests on POL-NS-01(d)/(b) and POL-NS-06. On the profile points: the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not tripped (no_show_terminations_30d = 1 against 120 completed trips, a rate of 0.008, below the 0.08 rate limb as well as the count of 4), so no payout is withheld - and, equally, none is due, because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full.

The money: EV-FARE-00403 shows one cancellation_fee line of $4.00, total_charged $4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd $0.00, so the whole contested $4.00 is returned. The monetary effect ($4.00) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of $8.00 and executes on issue. No referral is produced: no clause that adds one to a monetary ruling fires here - POL-NS-05 cannot be run without the driver's distance and speed at the arrival timestamp, the arrival was not platform-confirmed under POL-NS-12, and no stationary hold inside the arrival radius is established. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts are carried by EV-TRIP-00403, EV-GPS-00403 and EV-CHAT-00403, each at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00403-01, weight 0.0) carries no deciding fact and does not lower it, and the claim resting on it was discarded for citing an impaired artifact without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code; it is not reinstated.

ledger.claim: The chat log shows what actually happened. The rider's message sent at 13:27:32 named her exact position - 'taxi stand outside tower b basement 1' - which is the registered pickup point on the trip record (Westgate, 3 Gateway Dr, Jurong East, Taxi Stand Tower B B1, venue VEN-WESTGATE). The driver's reply at 13:28:07 placed him at 'the pickup bay near jem side' and told her to 'come over'; four minutes later he cancelled without moving. On those facts POL-NS-03 gives the rider the full refund, and limb (i) is directly on point: where the rider stated the correct entrance, block or tower in the chat log and the driver did not move to it before cancelling, the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii)'s pin-ambiguity goodwill is not open either, because it applies only where neither party specified a sub-location and this rider named the stand, the tower and the basement level. POL-NS-04's 120 second exoneration does not apply because the driver did reply, in 35 seconds - and POL-NS-04 itself sends a replied-to mislocation to POL-NS-03.

Any suggestion that the rider was not there is contradicted by her own track on the same artifact as the driver's. The rider track runs from 13:26:52 to 13:32:34 with 39 fixes, all 39 of them qualifying, a mean distance of 11.3 m from the pickup pin and a maximum of only 15.2 m, at a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph. That is squarely inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider presence radius, and it is stationary for the whole window down to the cancellation. The rider was at the pin and never left it; the driver was elsewhere and told her to move to him.

The driver cannot shortcut the geofence test with the platform's own arrival machinery. platform_policy.arrival_marker for this trip is BUTTON, not GPS_AUTO. POL-NS-12 recognises platform-confirmed arrival only from a GPS_AUTO arrival event carrying the platform's own geofence measurement with wait-timer events, and says in terms that a driver-pressed marker is not covered by it. The 13:26:52 'arrived' event is therefore nothing more than the driver's own assertion, which must be tested under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05 - and it does not survive the POL-NS-02 test set out above.

There is no money for the driver on this record. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Limb (d) fails, and POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 each displace it independently, so the 80 percent payout is never reached. POL-NS-03(i) separately denies compensation where the rider named the tower in chat and the driver did not move to it. Nothing in the driver's profile changes that: the anti-farming check requires no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more and a rate above 0.08, and the driver's figure is 1, so the profile is neither a ground for nor against anyone here.

Nothing on the rider's side of this case is impaired, so no discount applies to the facts that decide it. EV-GPS-00403 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 73 fixes at the 10 second expected cadence, 100 per cent coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so POL-NS-08(b)'s 120 second gap threshold and six-fix threshold are not engaged, and the rider track it relies on is present. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the deciding facts carry weight 1.0, and nothing here drives confidence to the 0.70 floor.

The sum in issue is exactly $4.00 and there is nothing else on the ledger. The fare breakdown shows a single cancellation_fee line of 4.00 against total_charged of 4.00, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the waiting_time_fee line at 0.00 with no distance, time or platform components. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line, and under POL-GEN-03 a ruling that returns the whole contested amount to the filing party - here the rider - is FULL_REFUND, meaning the present charge is not left standing.

This case should be decided, not deferred. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged: the driver's trace and the trip record are both COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and are not impaired under any limb of POL-NS-08, so limb (e) does not fire; the reason code in limb (d) of POL-NS-01 decides the charge whatever the arrival facts are, so there is no unresolved conflict of the kind limb (b) describes; and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 with rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d at 0, so limbs (c) and (d) do not fire. Escalation would only hold the $4.00 the rider has already been charged; the record supports a ruling now.

The platform's own trip record, not a reconstruction, places the driver at the pickup from 13:26:52 to the cancellation at 13:32:40 — a recorded wait of 5.8 minutes, i.e. 348 seconds, against the 300-second free waiting period in force for this LARGE_VENUE pickup under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec. On the record that levied the fee, the waiting period the rider was charged for was served, and limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is met on the platform's own measurement and not merely on the driver's assertion.

The rider's case rests on the derived arrival counter, and that counter does not affirmatively put the driver away from the pickup. The same artifact records the driver's nearest approach to the pin as 19.8 m (derived.driver_track.min_distance_m) while its arrival block records zero qualifying in-radius fixes (derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count = 0) against an arrival radius of 120 m for this zone class. Both numbers come from one trace and can be reconciled only by the horizontal-accuracy datum, which this package nowhere publishes; POL-NS-02 provides that a fix with no reported horizontal accuracy is evidence of neither presence nor absence, and the counter therefore cannot be read as a finding that the driver was elsewhere.

Two admissible artifacts, each COMPLETE at weight 1.0, state two different dwell figures — the trip record's 348 recorded seconds and the trace's 0-second longest qualifying run (derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec). The clause that would break that tie, POL-NS-05, cannot be run on this package, because it turns on the driver's distance from the pin and his speed at the 13:26:52 arrival marker and the package reports neither. Where two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on dwell and no clause resolves the conflict, POL-NS-09(b) sends the case to a human reviewer and the disputed fee is held rather than refunded while that review is pending.

This is the wrong-face-of-the-venue case POL-NS-03 was written for, not a driver who never came. The venue is recorded with three registered pickup points (trip_record.registered_pickup_points = 3); the rider's own track sits at the pin throughout, 39 of 39 qualifying fixes and never more than 15.17 m from it (derived.rider_presence.max_distance_m); and the driver told the rider in chat that he was at a pickup bay 'near jem side', a bay she was not at. The mislocation is a venue and pin question to be allocated from the chat log, where the driver stated where he was and kept waiting, rather than an absence.

The driver did not leave the rider uncoordinated. Her locating message was sent at 13:27:32 and the driver answered it at 13:28:07, 35 seconds later, telling her where he was; he messaged again at 13:30:52 and she read it at 13:31:12. POL-NS-04 exonerates a rider only where limb (b) holds — no reply within 120 seconds and no in-app call recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls — so limb (b) fails on this chat log and the fee cannot be disposed of on the footing that the driver ignored the rider.

Nothing in the driver's record supports an anti-farming inference. One no-show termination in the trailing 30 days against 120 completed trips is a rate of 0.008, an order of magnitude below the 0.08 that POL-NS-07 requires in addition to a count of 4 or more; both limbs of that check must hold, and neither does. No withholding of any payout is available against this driver, and no escalation under POL-NS-09 is available on the two profile counters POL-GEN-01 permits for this test.
